name: Jabil
key_signal: JBL has plunged 19.8% in a month (RSI 31.9, deeply oversold) despite still trading above its rising 200-day average with a forward P/E of just 18x against 27.6% expected earnings growth.
thesis: The stock's sharp 21-day drawdown looks like a valuation reset rather than a broken trend: it remains above its 200-day SMA (272.9) with an intact golden cross, and 126-day momentum is still solidly positive (+24.8%), suggesting the primary uptrend (driven by AI/data-center power and cooling demand for its EMS business) hasn't reversed. Forward P/E of 17.97 versus trailing P/E of 37.7 implies the market is pricing a large step-up in earnings, consistent with the reported 27.6% earnings growth and 11.8% revenue growth. RSI at 31.9 and a large gap below the 50-day SMA (356 vs 301 spot) point to an oversold condition ripe for mean reversion, and sell-side sentiment remains 'buy' even with only 9 analysts covering, meaning any recovery narrative has room to be re-rated before broader coverage catches up.
bear_case: The magnitude of the selloff (-19.7% in a month, MACD histogram sharply negative at -5.4, price now below the 50-day SMA by over 15%) could reflect a genuine deterioration in the AI/data-center capex cycle or a customer concentration issue rather than noise, and EMS businesses are notoriously thin-margin (gross margin just 9.2%, operating margin 5.2%, net margin 2.6%) so any revenue miss flows straight through to earnings. Debt-to-equity of 297% and a price-to-book of nearly 24x (largely an artifact of aggressive buybacks shrinking equity) leave the balance sheet with little cushion and the stock priced for perfection if growth disappoints. With only 9 analysts covering and beta of 1.28 in a name already showing 51% annualized volatility, negative surprises could compound quickly with limited institutional support to arrest the slide.
